calc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
calc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match).

calc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
calc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.
calc.preferred_translation: ရေအလျင်နှုန်း

calc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators.
calc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term.

ip.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
ip.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred.

ip.context: A drip irrigation emitter (dripper/micro-sprinkler) that delivers water at a controlled low flow rate directly to the soil or plant root zone. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the field term most familiar to irrigation practitioners in the target language. Arabic: 'قطارة' (dripper) is the field term, preferred over the academic 'مُصدِر'. Spanish: 'gotero' is field-common in Latin America alongside the technical 'emisor'. Ukrainian: 'крапельниця' is the field term used by irrigation workers.
ip.preferred_translation: ရေထုတ်ကိရိယာ

ip.context: Ratio of minimum to average emitter flow rate in a drip or sprinkler system. DU = q_min / q_avg. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: Use the irrigation engineering standard term. 'Uniformity' refers to how evenly water is distributed across the field, not physical evenness of the system. When the source says 'low-quarter DU', see the separate 'low-quarter distribution uniformity' entry. Hebrew: אחידות — never the nonword הוודות (found in shipped he file).

ip.context: Irrigation statistic: average of the lowest quarter of measured emitter flows divided by the overall average. Referenced in Irrigation Pressure notes as "textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity".
ip.translation_notes: Use the established irrigation-engineering phrase; do not invent one. "Textbook" is an adjective meaning "as defined in standard textbooks" — fr rendered it "manuel" (manual check), wrong. he: uniformity = אחידות, never the nonword הוודות.

ip.context: Depth of water applied per unit time by a drip or sprinkler system. PR = q / A_e. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.
ip.translation_notes: In irrigation, 'application rate' or 'precipitation rate' (for sprinklers) or 'irrigation rate'. Use the field irrigation term. Do not use a water-quality or chemical-application connotation.

ip.context: Irrigation branch line carrying emitters, fed by the mainline. Pairs with "mainline". Appears throughout Irrigation Pressure.
ip.translation_notes: Branch pipe of a drip/sprinkler system — NOT the adjective "side/lateral". Wrong renderings found: sw "taji" (crown). fr irrigation standard is "rampe". Keep one word per language and never alternate (it file mixed "laterale" and "manichetta").

ip.context: The trunk/supply pipe feeding the laterals in an irrigation system. Pairs with "lateral".
ip.translation_notes: Translate "main/mainline" as the trunk pipe, not the adjective "main". fr file left "main" untranslated ("Tronçons Main") — wrong.

ip.context: A segment of pipe or channel between two nodes/cross-sections. Table rows in Irrigation Pressure are reaches.
ip.translation_notes: Hydraulics noun, NOT "arrival/reaching" (ps "رسیدل" wrong), NOT "agent" (sw "mwakala" wrong), NOT "stripe" (km wrong).
ip.preferred_translation: ပိုက်အပိုင်း

ip.context: Kinetic energy per unit weight, V²/2g — a height of water column.
ip.translation_notes: "Head" is a height of water column, never anatomical (cs "rychlostní hlava" wrong — use "rychlostní výška").

ip.context: Head loss along the pipe due to wall friction (Darcy-Weisbach). Irrigation Pressure table column.
Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (K_m coefficient). Irrigation Pressure table column.
The total-head line (elevation + pressure head + velocity head) along a pipe or channel. Appears in Irrigation Pressure Method note.
ip.translation_notes: Use the established hydraulics term for the total-head line. ip.preferred_translation: စွမ်းအင်မျဉ်း

ip.translation_notes: Never software "downgrade". ar: downstream = المصب / أسفل المجرى (a file used المنبعية = source-side, wrong).

keys_to_translate.ip_main_title: Free Online Irrigation Pressure & Distribution Uniformity Calculator
keys_to_translate.ip_main_desc: Test Branch Pressure and Uniformity Estimate
keys_to_translate.ip_x: Emitter discharge exponent, x ?
keys_to_translate.ip_is_lateral: Lat. ?
keys_to_translate.ip_count: Emitters ?
keys_to_translate.ip_km: Km ?
keys_to_translate.ip_elev_ds: DS Elev. ?
keys_to_translate.ip_hl: Hl ?
keys_to_translate.ip_q_supply: Test path supply flow, Qsupply ?
keys_to_translate.ip_dp_avg: Est. Δpressure, avg. vs. test lateral ?
keys_to_translate.ip_q_avg_field: Est. field-average emitter flow, qavg,field ?
keys_to_translate.ip_du_estimate: Uniformity check, qlast/qavg,field ?
keys_to_translate.ip_q_ratio: Last emitter flow vs. design flow, qlast/qdesign ?
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_1_def: Guesses the pressure at the last (most remote) emitter, then marches the Energy Grade Line back toward the supply, reach by reach, adding friction and minor losses along the way. Elevation and velocity head are backed out at each node to report the actual pressure there. The guessed far-end pressure is adjusted (bisection) until the computed required supply pressure matches the entered supply pressure — the same closed-loop problem addressed by the pipe-flow solver on the Manning Pipe Flow calculator, extended to a branching network.
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_2_def: Each row is one reach along the single hydraulically worst path (the test path) from the supply to the last emitter. A Main reach only passes flow to laterals not on the test path, so its draw is a flat multiplication (design flow × the reach’s total emitter count) — no local pressure sensitivity. The main is a shared trunk pipe, so the reach right at the test lateral’s own takeoff must include not just laterals between its own endpoints but also any laterals still further down the main beyond that takeoff, or sharing the same junction (e.g. an opposite-side lateral) — their flow travels through that same reach before splitting off, whether or not they appear anywhere else in this table. A Lateral reach is a segment of the test lateral itself: emitter discharge is computed from the actual local pressure via q = k·H<sup>x</sup>, and friction loss is reduced by Christiansen’s F(n) factor to account for flow stepping down as each emitter in the reach draws off.
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_3_def: Models one fixed inlet pressure (no pump curve), one test path only (not the full field), and a 2-parameter emitter curve (set the exponent near 0 to approximate a pressure-compensating emitter). Two different ratios are reported, deliberately kept separate: q<sub>last</sub>/q<sub>avg,field</sub> is a uniformity check, shaped like textbook low-quarter Distribution Uniformity (low-group average ÷ population mean) but computed from the test lateral’s own modeled emitters, corrected by an entered Δpressure estimate rather than a full-field statistical sample — the test lateral is deliberately the presumed worst case, so its raw, uncorrected average would understate the true field average and make uniformity look better than it is; the Δpressure input exists specifically to counter that bias. Values at or above 1 are still possible (e.g. the Δpressure estimate is too small, or a favorable downhill run). q<sub>last</sub>/q<sub>design</sub> is a different, non-uniformity check against the manufacturer’s rated flow — useful for spotting an over- or under-pressured system overall, but not a substitute for the uniformity number, since the design/rated flow has no necessary relationship to the system’s actual mean operating pressure.
keys_to_translate.ip_notes_5_def: Application rate and system/zone flow use the estimated field-average emitter flow (q<sub>avg,field</sub> — the test lateral’s own average, corrected by the entered Δpressure estimate), not a guessed rate: PR = q<sub>avg,field</sub> / A<sub>e</sub>, fed by the corrected modeled value. Spacing and system-wide lateral/emitter counts are separate inputs here because the test path only models one worst-case branch, not every lateral in the field.
keys_to_translate.irr_card_pressure_desc: Model the pressure and flow profile along a main-lateral-emitter branch to estimate distribution uniformity from the real test-path pressure, not just a catalog emitter flow rate.

key_intent.ip_main_menu: Pressure in a pressurized irrigation system (drip or sprinkler pipe network).
key_intent.ip_main_title: Pressure in a pressurized drip/sprinkler irrigation network. Uniformity means evenness of water application among emitters, an irrigation-engineering statistic.
key_intent.ip_main_desc: Pressure in a branch of study and estimate of distribution uniformity.
key_intent.ip_x: Discharge exponent: the exponent x in q = k*H^x describing emitter hydraulic behavior. Discharge here is water outflow, never electrical.
key_intent.ip_group_upstream: Direction along the water path: upstream = toward the supply. Hydraulics term, not a software term (never upgrade).
key_intent.ip_group_downstream: Direction along the water path: downstream = toward the last emitter. Hydraulics term, not a software term (never downgrade).
key_intent.ip_is_lateral: Main = the mainline or trunk pipe; lateral = the branch line carrying emitters. Test = the path being analyzed, not a default. Use established drip-irrigation terms.
key_intent.ip_count: Lateral = branch line with emitters; main = trunk pipe. The reach right at the takeoff means exactly at that location, not the right-hand side. Branch (verb) means to split off flow.
key_intent.ip_elev_ds: DS abbreviates downstream. Choose an abbreviation that is unambiguously downstream and cannot be confused with upstream.
key_intent.ip_hv: Symbol: velocity head. Keep H and the subscript exactly as in English. Head is a height of water column, never anatomical.
key_intent.ip_hf: Symbol: friction head loss. Keep H and the subscript exactly as in English.
key_intent.ip_hm: Symbol: minor (local) head loss. Keep H and the subscript exactly as in English.
key_intent.ip_hl: Symbol: total reach head loss. Keep H and the subscript exactly as in English.
key_intent.ip_q_supply: Keep the subscript supply exactly as in English; subscripted names are symbols.
key_intent.ip_q_avg_field: Keep the subscripts avg,field exactly as in English; subscripted names are symbols.
key_intent.ip_du_estimate: Low-quarter Distribution Uniformity is the irrigation-engineering statistic DU_lq: average of the lowest quarter of measurements divided by the overall average. Use the established irrigation term in the target language; do not invent a phrase.
key_intent.ip_notes_1_def: Technical hydraulics prose. Key senses: a reach is a pipe segment between two nodes, not an arrival or extent. To draw or draw off means to withdraw water. The reach right at the takeoff means the reach located exactly at that point, not the right-hand side. Energy Grade Line is the standard hydraulics term for the total-head line; use the established term in the target language, never a word-by-word calque. Textbook (adjective) means as defined in standard textbooks, not a manual. A favorable downhill run means the pipe descends, gaining elevation head. Bisection is the numerical root-finding method. Keep symbols q_last, q_avg,field, q_design, k, H, x, F(n) exactly as written.
